newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil closes sharply lower on inventory data.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil closes sharply lower on inventory data.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures closed sharply lower on Wednesday after U.S. weekly stock data showed tanks were filling up with heating oil and weather patterns suggested no immediate surge in demand for physical supplies, brokers said.
November gas oil closed $6 a tonne lower at $217.25 a tonne.
The American Petroleum Institute said on Tuesday that total distillate supplies grew 3.6 million barrels for the week ended October 25.
Heating oil stocks gained 1.6 million barrels with distillate production at a record 3.8 million barrels a day.
Dealers said output had outstripped demand due to warmer weather in the key northeast U.S. market.

Gas oil's weakness was not entirely mirrored by Brent crude oil futures, which weakened earlier in the day but managed to scramble to a high of $23.65 a barrel later on some short-covering and buy stops, brokers said.
NYMEX unleaded gasoline, which has gone its own way in the last few days on tight supplies confirmed by the API, managed to undo some of the damage from weaker gas oil.
"Gasoline has been positive most of the day. Heating oil is dragging crude down and gasoline is holding it up.
"That's why the market is going up and down like a ho-yo," a broker said.
IPE December crude was trading 24 cents down at $23.51 a barrel at 1804 GMT.
